topic: The Physics of Pi: Colliding Blocks and Digit Emergence
target_audience: Undergraduate Physics Students or Curious High School Students

sections.title: The Hook: An Unexpected Connection
lecture_lines: Colliding blocks can calculate digits of Pi.
Tiny block bounces off a massive block.
The number of collisions matches Pi digits.
animations: Display text 'Colliding blocks calculate digits of Pi' in #FFFFFF.
Fade in two blocks of different sizes in #FF5733 and #33FF57.
Animate a single collision between the two blocks.

sections.title: Prerequisite Physics: Conservation Laws
lecture_lines: Elastic collisions conserve momentum and kinetic energy.
State follows an ellipse of constant energy.
Velocities swap during perfectly elastic bounces.
animations: Animate velocity exchange upon bounce in #33FF57.

sections.title: Mapping Collisions to Geometry
lecture_lines: Represent the state as a single ray.
Bounces map to reflections within a wedge.
animations: Map 1D motion to a 2D ray path in #FF5733.
Render reflection lines within a geometric wedge in #33FF57.
Highlight reflection points on the wedge walls.

sections.title: The Limit of Mass Ratios
lecture_lines: Mass ratios dictate the wedge angle size.
As mass grows, reflections trace an arc.
The arc length corresponds to value Pi.
animations: Plot mass ratio impact on wedge angle in #FFFFFF.
Draw arc representing path of reflection in #FFC300.
Highlight final arc length related to Pi in #FF5733.

sections.title: Conclusion and Intuition
lecture_lines: Collisions track angle in phase space.
Pi emerges from geometric physical constraints.
Blocks act as a physical calculation engine.
animations: Display final phase space visual in #FFFFFF.
Overlay conclusion text about Pi calculation in #FFC300.
Animate blocks fading into a final geometric shape.
